text.p: These are the leading stories in the Egyptian press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Group of Seven industrial countries vow to push forward the Middle East peace process. The Denver summit asks Israel not to jump ahead of the final status negotiations. U.S. President Bill Clinton promises to get the peace process out of the dead end it is currently in. Foreign Minister Amr Moussa says the gap is very wide between the Israelis and the Palestinians.
- Arab tourism ministers hold meetings today in Cairo to discuss establishing a bank and common market as well as boosting tourism.
- Foreign ministers of the Damascus Declaration countries meet in Syria the day after tomorrow to discuss the final wording of the Arab common market document.

- Prime Minister Kamal Ganzouri says the country must strike a balance between local and international investment. State approves plans for a huge agricultural firm in East Oweinat with a capital of one billion pounds ($295 million). Construction of Dakhla and East Oweinat airports and the Toshka road to end within two weeks.
- C.N.N. lauds President Mubarak's role in supervising the education system.
- Italian television says the New Valley project is the largest project of this era.
- Makram Mohammad Ahmed is voted in as the new head of the journalists syndicate.
- Prosecution bans four people charged with smuggling secondary school exams from travelling.
- A fire guts the kidney dialysis unit of the Kasr el-Aini hospital, no casualties.
- German police investigating the death of an EgyptAir official in Frankfurt.
